subject: Residency activation criteria + network safeguards (EU/APAC private deploy)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Paul Sweeney <paul.sweeney@horizonbank.com>; Horizon Bank Security <security@horizonbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency activation criteria + network safeguards (EU/APAC private deploy)

Hi Paul / Horizon security team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached are the draft "Residency Activation Criteria" and a complementary network safeguards diagram for the planned private deployment across our EU private region with an APAC warm-standby. Key points to review:

- Activation criteria (page 1 of PDF): explicit list of triggers for switching custody/traffic (legal directive, region outage, capacity saturation >95% for >30m).
- KMS / key residency: we propose dual-envelope encryption — customer KMS in EU (primary) + Redwood-hosted wrap key in EU only; no key material leaves EU jurisdiction during normal operations.
- Egress gating and permitted peering: transit will be via a dedicated transit VPC peered to customer VPCs with ACLs and explicit BGP communities.
- Failover behavior: traffic will failover from EU to APAC warm-standby only when activation criteria are met AND approval token (2-person ops signoff) is provided. Fallback to Redwood-hosted tier (hosted API) is available as a last resort but only after documented legal/CS approval.

Please review the KMS matrix and the proposed cutover window constraints in the spreadsheet; we called out required audit artifacts we can provide (KMS access logs, VPC flow logs, control-plane audit trail).

Attachments: residency-activation-criteria-v1.pdf, network-safeguards-diagram.vsdx, kms-key-residency-matrix.xlsx

Ask: can you confirm whether Horizon requires a separate EU-only HSM (customer-provided) for production? Also please flag any additional regulatory gate triggers (e.g., local regulator notice windows) we should model in the activation criteria.

If helpful we can schedule a short table-top next week and run through an example failover timeline.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com]

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Paul Sweeney <paul.sweeney@horizonbank.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency activation criteria + network safeguards (EU/APAC private deploy)

Thanks for putting this together, Jasmine — good, concrete start. A few internal notes and one question for Horizon inline: 

1) Dual-KMS recommendation: we should call out an explicit tie-break for a compromised EU KMS key: policy must state whether APAC warm-standby should be able to unwrap tokens (we recommend NO, unless judicially compelled). Recommend adding a manual override flow with legal/CS approval.

2) Cutover window and RTO: the doc lists a 30-minute detection window. For production workloads we need to clarify expected RTO and RPO for the customer's top-of-funnel endpoints; suggest we add an SLT (service-level target) section: RTO 15-30m for control-plane failover, RPO = last successful checkpointed KV-cache update.

3) Network safeguards: add explicit DENY-by-default NACL templates and note that all inter-region BGP announcements from Redwood will include community tags that Horizon will filter at their edge. Also call out BGP session TTL and MD5 auth if required.

4) Audit artifacts: we can provide a signed snapshot of VPC flow logs and a signed KMS event bundle for the cutover window. Confirm with Horizon whether signed bundles meet their audit requirements or if they require on-site physical evidence.

Question for Horizon (Paul): do you require our control plane logs to be exported to a Horizon-managed SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery) in real-time, or will nightly exports suffice for now?

I'm proposing a short tabletop on Thu (EU-friendly window) to walk through a failover scenario where the EU primary goes into an extended maintenance and we must preserve custody semantics.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Paul Sweeney <paul.sweeney@horizonbank.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Bank Security <security@horizonbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency activation criteria + network safeguards (EU/APAC private deploy)

Hi Jasmine / team —

Thanks for the materials. A few quick answers and follow-ups from Horizon: 

- HSM requirement: for PCI/regulatory reasons at some of our higher-risk segments, we do require EU-resident HSM-backed keys managed by us. We will need an integration plan for our on-prem HSM (Thales) to wrap/un-unwrap tokens; can Redwood provide a KMS gateway or accept wrapped keys during onboarding?

- SIEM integration: we need near-real-time exports (<5m) of control-plane security events for the first 90 days after cutover. Nightly exports are insufficient for our compliance team.

- Failover semantics: we appreciate the two-person ops signoff. One clarification — regulators in our APAC markets explicitly disallow automatic failover that changes data custody without prior notification. For those accounts, we will require a simulated failover rehearsal and a formal registrar entry before any switch that changes custody jurisdiction.

We will review the KMS matrix and return redlines by Friday. For the Thales integration, I will loop in our HSM lead — forwarding thread.

Regards,
Paul
Head of Cloud Engineering — Horizon Bank

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency activation criteria + network safeguards (EU/APAC private deploy)

Team — quick summary and next steps to lock this down for Horizon: 

1) HSM integration: action item for Redwood infra (Karthik) to propose a Thales gateway pattern or documented wrapped-key onboarding flow by Tue 21 Jul. Deliverable: technical runbook + test harness.

2) SIEM exports: we will implement near-real-time (<5m) control-plane event pushes to Horizon SIEM for the first 90 days; Security to confirm throughput/truncation limits. (So-ji n to own config).

3) Activation & rehearsal: Horizon requires a documented rehearsal and registrar entry prior to any custody-altering failover. We will schedule a table-top for Wed 22 Jul (EU window) and a live rehearsal in a dark-green environment in August. Jasmine will send invites + updated docs.

4) Audit artifacts: Redwood will include signed KMS event bundles + VPC flow log snapshot for every rehearsal/cutover. Legal will pre-approve the bundle format.

5) Decision log: create an entry in HubSpot (link: https://hubspot.company/recs/HB-2026-PRV-09) and mark this thread as the residency activation working record.

I'll prepare a short customer-facing one-pager capturing these five points and attach the updated runbook once Karthik's draft is in. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

Marissa Cole
Director, Deployments — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
